verdict.rationale: Supabase Auth documents a Custom Access Token Hook that adds, removes or changes JWT claims, so developer-defined role data can appear in session tokens. It also documents the auth token scoping database access row-by-row when combined with RLS policies, which gives enforcement. However, there is no documented first-party model for defining roles and permissions; developers store them in their own tables and wire them in through hooks and Postgres policies, and one community member asked which external AuthZ provider to pair with it. Missing for 10: a built-in role/permission definition and management model, documented RBAC enforcement beyond RLS wiring, and independent or hands-on corroboration of an RBAC setup.

support.subject: As a developer, I can define roles and permissions and have them enforced and surfaced in session tokens for authorization checks

citations.quote: You can use a [Custom Access Token Hook](/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook) to add, remove or change claims present in the token.
The Auth Token scopes database access on a row-by-row level when used along with [RLS policies](/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security).
Customize Auth behavior with Postgres functions at key lifecycle points.
